## Role in the Rating Process

The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development supplies data that supports the assessment of [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd). Specifically, its Global Debt Report serves as the fallback source for estimating average maturity and bill stocks (R1-E*).

## Evidence by Country

### [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd)

- The report references OECD analysis on education and skills strategies, calculations of the tax wedge, and assessments of regulatory policy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 26, p. 49, p. 74" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 26, p. 49, p. 74">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD Economic Outlook 118 database serves as the primary source for macroeconomic projections for Bulgaria. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 10" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- The report estimates that structural reforms could raise per capita gross domestic product by 9% by 2060. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that at current growth rates, it would take 28 years for Bulgaria to converge to average OECD income levels. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The report highlights that unit labour costs have tripled since European Union accession, eroding the country's cost advantage. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 117" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 117">ⓘ</button>
- The report recommends front-loaded fiscal consolidation to narrow the deficit and maintain the current debt ratio. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The report estimates that reducing corruption to Visegrad-4 levels would raise per capita gross domestic product by 2.1% in the long run. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 135" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 135">ⓘ</button>
- The report projects that without policy adjustments, the government debt ratio would rise to 160% by 2060. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 54">ⓘ</button>

### [Cyprus](../countries/cyprus.qmd)

- The report cites OECD data on tax wedge calculations and better regulation practices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, pp. 35, 61" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, pp. 35, 61">ⓘ</button>

### [Finland](../countries/finland.qmd)

- The OECD published an [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd) in May 2025, providing macroeconomic forecasts for [Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd), [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd), [Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd), and [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 11, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 11, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- The report identifies a fragile recovery in real gross domestic product, projected to grow modestly in 2025 and 2026, lagging behind Nordic peers and the OECD average. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that productivity growth has weakened significantly, attributed to the collapse of Nokia, the end of trade with Russia, and firms remaining too small. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 24" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- The report highlights downside risks skewed by geopolitical tensions, cyber-attacks, and trade policy uncertainty. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The report states that the general government fiscal balance deteriorated to -4.4% of gross domestic product in 2023 and is projected to improve slightly to -3.7% in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that recent tax cuts and increased defense budgets announced in April 2025 threaten to slow fiscal consolidation progress. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 12" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- The report emphasizes the need for increased spending efficiency, particularly in health and social care, and structural reforms to boost labor market participation. [oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23]
- The report projects that gross general government debt will rise from 85.6% of gross domestic product in 2023 to 96.3% in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- The report indicates that defense spending has risen rapidly and is targeted to increase to 3% of gross domestic product by 2029, contributing to debt accumulation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The report estimates that without further reforms, public debt would reach 151% of gross domestic product by 2050 in the baseline scenario. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The report references the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s assessment and OECD projections on the need for continued fiscal consolidation to ensure debt sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that consumer and business confidence remain subdued, particularly in the construction sector. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The report identifies significant security risks from Russia, including cyber-attacks and infrastructure sabotage, as contributors to economic uncertainty. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The report states that the working-age population is projected to shrink in the 2030s under baseline migration assumptions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses its Economic Outlook Database for short-term projections and its Long-Term Model for medium- and long-term simulations. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD estimates the structural deficit and projects the general government fiscal balance based on policy assumptions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD simulations assess the long-term trajectory of debt under different policy and demographic scenarios. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD’s Product Market Regulation indicators and economic surveys are used to benchmark Finland's competitiveness and administrative barriers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 7, p. 117, p. 120" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 7, p. 117, p. 120">ⓘ</button>

### [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd)

- The report cites the OECD 2024 [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd) for Greece and the 2025 Regulatory Policy Outlook, providing data on tax wedges, corporate income tax gaps, and regulatory practices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 41, p. 44, p. 67-68, p. 94" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 41, p. 44, p. 67-68, p. 94">ⓘ</button>

### [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd)

- The report cites OECD data and assessments on better regulation practices, tax wedges, and productivity. The OECD has published an [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd) of Ireland recommending stronger fiscal frameworks and spending reviews. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 35, p. 59" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 35, p. 59">ⓘ</button>

### [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd)

- The OECD published an [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd) in April 2025, providing macroeconomic forecasts for [Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd), [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd), [Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd), and [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The report identifies a gradual recovery in real gross domestic product, projected to grow by 2.1% in 2025 and 2.3% in 2026, supported by easing financial conditions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that measured labor productivity has stagnated since 2010, driven by declining multi-factor productivity and slowing capital deepening. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 80-82" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 80-82">ⓘ</button>
- The report highlights that unit labor costs increased by about 15% since the end of 2021, leading to an appreciation in the unit labor cost-based real effective exchange rate. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- The report states that the government budget balance is projected to be -0.0% of gross domestic product in 2025 and -0.1% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that gross public debt was 24.9% of gross domestic product in 2023 and is projected to rise slightly to 23.5% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The report emphasizes the need for comprehensive pension reforms, as the current system is projected to become unsustainable by the late 2040s without changes. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- The report projects that gross pension expenditure will rise from 9.4% of gross domestic product in 2024 to 17.5% in 2070 without reform. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- The report indicates that net financial debt was -48.2% of gross domestic product in 2023, indicating a strong net creditor position. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 7" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 7">ⓘ</button>
- The report recommends adopting a national net spending rule to anchor fiscal policy and enhance the mandate of the national fiscal council. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, p. 46">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD’s Product Market Regulation indicators and economic surveys are used to benchmark Luxembourg's competitiveness and administrative barriers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 14, 53" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 14, 53">ⓘ</button>

### [Spain](../countries/spain.qmd)

- The report cites OECD data on skills shortages, productivity, and tax policy. The OECD notes that 66% of Spanish small and medium-sized enterprises report difficulties hiring staff with appropriate skills. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 44" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 44">ⓘ</button>
- The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development reports that lack of available financing is a considerable long-term barrier to investment for Spanish firms, notably small and medium-sized enterprises. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 8" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 8">ⓘ</button>
